rationale:
structural: The requirement's text prescribes one structural obligation: the signature `pub fn node_id(&self) -> &NodeId<D>` on `impl<'d, D: Domain> ValidationContext<'d, D>`. It also says the method borrows the identity of the source node being checked.

An alternative that returned `NodeId<D>` by value, or cloned it, could produce the same node identity at run time. It would still violate the prescribed borrowed-return signature, so this clause is a real structural obligation.

The root is `crates/trust-but-verify/src/procedure.rs#impl[ValidationContext<'d, D>]#1/fn[node_id]`. It is declared as `pub fn node_id(&self) -> &NodeId<D>` and returns `&self.node`. That matches the prescribed signature and borrows the stored node identity without copying it. The root carries the `{impl}` marker for this requirement.

I found no other structural obligation and no missing root.

behavioral: The only observable obligation is that `ValidationContext::node_id` returns a borrow of the identity of the source node being checked. `crates/trust-but-verify/src/graph/validation_tests.rs#fn[labeled_selections_track_only_target_membership_without_reading_contents]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. It builds `ValidationContext::new(&graph, graph.cache().intern_node(1))` and asserts `ctx.node_id() == &graph.cache().intern_node(1)`. The test also queries other nodes (9, and 1 as a target), so a `node_id` that returned the wrong node would be caught. Node 1 is the context's subject, and the other nodes differ from it.

The `&NodeId<D>` signature is a compile-time property. The test uses it by comparing against a reference, and `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/public_api.rs#fn[public_exports_match_the_appendix]` covers the public API inventory. The requirement adds no other behavioral obligations, so I found no gaps.
